name: Abstractive-Summarization
description: The Abstractive-Summarization dataset contains news articles paired with concise, abstractive one-sentence summaries. It evaluates a model's ability to read a full document and generate a faithful, condensed summary in its own words.
card_text: This dataset is a text-to-text abstractive summarization benchmark. Each sample consists of a long English news article stored under the 'document' field and a short summary stored under 'output.summary'. The articles cover real-world news topics such as crime, policing inquiries, sports matches, and public affairs. The target summaries are single sentences that capture the central event or outcome, often using paraphrased wording rather than extracted spans. The dataset assumes that models can process long input passages and produce concise, fluent summaries. It contains 201 samples, all in English, with no additional labels or multiple-choice options. The main challenge is faithful content selection and abstractive compression.

context.semantics: The full source news article to be summarized. It contains detailed reporting, background, quotations, and event descriptions about a specific news story.

answer.semantics: A concise abstractive summary of the document, usually one sentence, that captures the main point or outcome of the news article.

meta.meta_structure_description: Each sample contains a source document and a target summary. The 'document' field holds a long news article that provides the full context, while the nested 'output.summary' field holds a short, abstractive one-sentence summary of that article. The summary is a condensed paraphrase of the document's key information.
